items.title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve: Cryptographic Proofs That a Reply Came From Committed Weights - MarkTechPost
items.summary:
| Metrics | FlashProve | Attestable | VerInf | DeepProve | zkLLM |
 ---  ---  --- |
| Model proven | Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE) | Gemma 4 31B (dense) | Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE) | GPT-2, Gemma 3 | LLaMA-2-13B |
| Throughput | ~110 tok/s | 53 to 77 tok/s | ~0.02 tok/s (1,000 tokens in 14.3 h) | ~2.9 tok/s (GPT-2), ~1.4 tok/s (Gemma 3) | Full inference in under 15 min |
| Hardware | 1 H100 + 24 CPU cores | 1 H100 | 1 DGX Spark | 1 machine; 31 tok/s distributed | GPU (CUDA) | [...] Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team has released FlashProve, an open-source research prototype for provable inference. FlashProve is a zkSNARK system from Anthropic that proves a reply came from a committed model. The proof reveals nothing about the model weights. On Llama 4 Maverick, a 400B mixture-of-experts model, it proves about 110 tokens/second on 1 H100. For developers, this targets a real gap: today you cannot check which model actually answered your API call.

## TL;DR

items.title: Anthropic FlashProve: Provable Inference at 72x [2026]
items.summary:
## The Llama 4 Maverick Benchmark Against vLLM

Anthropic picked a hard target. Llama 4 Maverick is a 400-billion-parameter MoE model. That makes it a fair stress test for a system built for large MoE models. Readers tracking which open models are worth running can compare Maverick’s class against others in our open-weight AI models spec sheet. [...] Is FlashProve open source? Yes. The prover, two verifiers (one in C++, one in Lean), the formal proofs, and the protocol specification were released under the Apache 2.0 license. The Llama 4 Maverick weights are not included, and users obtain them separately. [...] How much slower is proving than normal inference? Against vLLM running Llama 4 Maverick in FP8 on eight H100 GPUs, the overhead was about 72 times per GPU across runs and about 94 times at the heaviest tested load. Secondary reports round this to 70 to 95 times, which Anthropic’s source does not state as a range.

FlashProve reaches 110 tokens per second on one H100, with proofs verifiable in seconds. The team released the code, technical report, protocol specification, and Lean proofs under the Apache 2.0 license. [...] The researchers tested the system on Llama 4 Maverick, a 400-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 4-bit quantized weights. A single H100 GPU produced proofs at 110 tokens per second. Each proof measured 18.78 megabytes per 1,024-token request.

Proof generation requires 70 to 95 times the GPU time that vLLM needs on eight H100s for the same requests. The offline commitment phase takes 39 minutes and remains valid for about 16 million requests. After that, the provider commits again.
